name: Douglas Murray
role: British author and commentator, associate editor of The Spectator
summary: Murray is a British conservative commentator who argues for sharply restricting mass migration, defends Western and Christian-heritage culture, and opposes identity politics, critical race theory and reparations. He supports gay marriage and free speech, defended the Iraq war, and is a strong supporter of Israel and Ukraine.

notes: Local phase: his four books in the maintainer library, the Lex Fridman #463 transcript and two Spectator pieces. Book passages found for the web phase (cite each book with its catalogue page): Strange Death of Europe, 'What might have been' (offshore asylum, deportation, temporary asylum: reduce-immigration +2; diversity in large numbers ends society: diversity-weakens-cohesion +1; Burke's pact: preserve-national-culture +2; blasphemy law demands a threat: punish-blasphemy -2; Asad Shah murder for apostasy: apostasy-punishable -2; 'tyranny of guilt', reparations and apologies: apologise-for-past-wrongs -1). Madness of Crowds: gay equality a great success (criminalize-homosexuality -2), intersectionality (intersecting-oppressions -2), Mill on free speech (restrict-hate-speech -1). War on the West: reparations would rip a society apart (slavery-reparations -2), West's culture and free market (cultures-equal-different -2, capitalism-progressive +1), CCP abuses (totalitarianisms-equivalent +1). Web phase: books cited through catalogue pages; Spectator and Free Press migration columns searched. Wikipedia-only answers on blasphemy, apostasy and communist/fascist equivalence stay null: no passage opened that settles them.
